newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai stocks plunge on poor sentiment after HK.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai stocks plunge on poor sentiment after HK.

text.p: Shanghai's foreign currency B shares and domestic currency A shares plunged on Monday due to weak sentiment after the return of Hong Kong to Chinese rule, brokers said.
The former British colony of Hong Kong reverted to Chinese rule on July 1, but despite the nationwide euphoria over the event, China's stock markets have fallen steadily since.
The B index closed down 2.080 points or 2.73 percent to 74.145 points on volume of 9.038 million shares worth $5.672 million.
"Investors rushed to sell despite taking losses," said a broker at a foreign securities firm in Shanghai. "There was no positive news to support the index."

The letdown after the Hong Kong handover, which had been a major postive factor supporting the market, also hit the A shares along with rumours of further government steps to keep the markets stable, brokers said.
The A index ended down 66.196 points or 5.46 percent at 1,145.251 points on volume of 335.038 million shares worth 4.098 billion yuan.
"Rumours of tighter curbs on speculation, which have circulated in the markets before, were heard again, triggering some panic selling," the foreign securities firm broker said.
Persistent rumours that the government will take further steps against state enterprises speculating in shares or list some types of non-traded shares have plagued the market in recent days.
In addition, a flood of expected listings on both the A and B markets had damaged sentiment as investors have turned away from existing shares to wait for the new issues, brokers said.
Regulators on Friday reaffirmed measures to chase domestic investors out of the B share market, which is technically limited to foreigners, hurting sentiment in Monday trading.
Of 45 B shares, 41 traded with 32 down, six flat and three up.
Shanghai Steel Tube Co 900926.SS was the biggest B share loser on expectations of poor interim results. It plunged $0.014 or 10.14 percent to $0.124.
Shanghai Lujiazui Finance & Trade Zone Development Co was the most actively traded with volume of 1.2 million shares. It fell $0.044 or 3.48 percent to $1.220.
Shanghai's SSE30 blue chip index slumped 218.491 points or 5.71 percent to 3,605.177 points.

Brokers said the market would continue to fall at a measured pace in the short term as investors looked for reasons to return to the market, such as the possible announcement of positive interim results later this month and in August.
In the longer term, investors were looking towards the 15th Chinese Communist Party congress, expected in October, which could provide clues on the development of China's economy.
The B share index could test support at 68 points in the next several days, brokers said.
